newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Dajiang sees lower profits for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Dajiang sees lower profits for 1996.

text.p: Shanghai Dajiang Co Ltd expects around 150 million yuan in operating profit for 1996, down from 236 million yuan in 1995, a company official said on Friday.
The Sino-Thai joint venture's net profit in 1995 was 198 million, up 9.92 percent on its 1994 profits of 180.1 million yuan. He gave no estimate for 1996 net profit.
The Thai partner is Chia Tai, a unit of Thailand's C.P. Pokphand.

Dajiang, a major producer of chicken meat and feedgrain, saw mid-year profits fall 37.8 percent to 58.58 million yuan from 94.25 million yuan in the same period of 1995 because of rising raw material prices, particularly corn.
But the company official said a fall in corn prices combined with higher export prices and satisfactory domestic sales had improved company performance in the second half of 1996.

Plans for project to raise 600,000 pigs per year had been shelved because of government concerns over environmental problems caused by large-scale pig farming in the densely populated Shanghai area, the official said.
"But the company is unable to move pork production elsewhere because of the need for the infrastructure and expertise available here in Shanghai," he added.
The official said he expected stable growth for the company in 1997, in step with the development of the national economy.
"Revival in domestic demand will probably be slow, increasing pressure on the company to export," he said.
Dajiang at present sells one-third of its poultry overseas.
